resources.string: SecureBrowse dedicated-device administrator. Used only after this app is intentionally provisioned as device owner.

A local passphrase is not device security. On a normal phone, someone who can uninstall this app or clear its storage can discard the allowlist. Keeping people inside this app requires Android Enterprise device-owner provisioning and lock task mode.

Homepage: none. Home shows this screen.
This passphrase protects the allowlist on this device. It is hashed with PBKDF2 and is not stored. It is not a device PIN, and it does not stop someone from using Chrome on an unmanaged phone.
Settings stay locked until this passphrase is accepted. The unlock lasts five minutes in memory and is forgotten when the process stops.
Enter the current passphrase and a new one. There is no recovery code.
The two entries do not match.
Too many attempts. Try again after the lockout ends.
Download this file from an approved site into the app’s private download folder?
This site usually needs more domains

Nothing is added unless you approve it. Third-party domains can run scripts in the page if resource blocking is off, or if you add them. googleusercontent.com also hosts content uploaded by other people.
This only works on test devices where device owner was set with adb. Production provisioning usually cannot be cleared without a factory reset. Continue?
Strict mode blocks USB debugging. If you lose the passphrase you may need a factory reset, and factory reset is also restricted. Continue?
These policies do nothing until SecureBrowse is the device owner. Installing the app does not make it the device owner.
Screen pinning asks the person holding the device to confirm. They can leave with Back and Recents. This is not kiosk mode.
The page process stopped. SecureBrowse stayed open and returned home.
The stored allowlist could not be decrypted. Navigation is fail-closed. Reset only if you accept losing the saved domains.
The administrator verifier could not be read. There is no backdoor. Clearing app storage is the unmanaged-device recovery, and it also deletes the allowlist.

During a session only SecureBrowse and the apps you select can stay in front, and only after this app is the device owner. Pull-down ban calls setStatusBarDisabled, which blocks the notification shade and quick settings. Notification ban turns off the lock-task notification feature. Neither one stops Chrome on a normal unlocked phone. Ending early needs this passphrase. Changing the app list applies to the next session, not the one already running.
